title: R GRID
subtitle: One grid, four layouts and four modules: a keyboard series designed in 2026
context: Personal project. A design, not built.
role: Direction and design, with AI tools for the drawings and renders
summary: A series of keyboards drawn on one 19.05 mm grid. The top of each is a black board with the grid printed on it; under it are a row of blue spacers, a white circuit board and a base of frosted acrylic. It uses the layouts, the feet and the hidden nuts of the keyboards I built in 2021 to 2023.

sections.heading: One grid
sections.body:
Every key in the series sits on a grid of 19.05 mm. Each board has a margin of 9.025 mm around its keys, and boards are set 1 mm apart, so two margins and a gap come to exactly one key. However the boards are arranged, the keys stay on the same grid.

The board on top is the face of the keyboard. What is printed on it is the grid itself: a tick and a number over every column, a letter beside every row, and the name of the board.

sections.heading: Four layouts
sections.body: The same construction on four of my own layouts: 64, 67 and 75 keys, and the Alice layout with its keys in two angled halves.

sections.heading: Boards that fit together
sections.body: The 64 takes a strip of fifteen keys above it, a number pad beside it, or a dial with six keys. The base is cut to the arrangement.

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.body:
From the desk up: a 3 mm base and a 5 mm frame of frosted acrylic, a white circuit board, a 2.2 mm spacer and the black board. Screws go in from the top; each nut is brass and sits in a six-sided pocket cut in the frame, the way I held the nuts in the stacked 64, so none shows from below or from the side. The feet are the ones from the thin 67: upright pieces held by two cross bolts.

There are four colours. Blue is used only for parts with a job: the spacers, the dial and the feet.

sections.heading: The keycap
sections.body: The keycap took a round of its own. Five were modelled and put on the same board. The one chosen is low, with a wide shallow dish, and leaves 2 mm of black board between keys.

sections.heading: Light
sections.body: The base is frosted, so light from under the circuit board spreads through it and comes out along the edge.
